A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain complete, readable main texts and Appendices A–D. Their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison; appendix pages 18–35 are identical.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification and scene-understanding experiments in Section 5, plus calibration, robustness and other empirical analyses in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original benchmark results and supplementary empirical analyses in Section 5 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: Sections 4.3–4.4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same SAM perturbations, separate aggregation of loss and flatness gradients, and parameter updates. No method component, objective or architecture changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MultiFashion, MultiMNIST, MultiFashion+MNIST, CelebA, CityScapes and NYUv2. The cross-domain tests between MultiMNIST and MultiFashion and other appendix scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain identical comparator membership, including MGDA, PCGrad, CAGrad, IMTL, STL and the additional baselines in Tables 2–4. The direct-aggregation comparison in Table 5 and IMTL/F-IMTL comparisons in Appendix D are unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C retain the same model configurations, preprocessing, training budgets, evaluation metrics and averaging over the final ten epochs for scene understanding. Appendix D's testing procedures also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendix D retain the same aggregation ablation, perturbation-radius sensitivity, gradient-conflict, noise-robustness, calibration, segmentation examples, loss-landscape and training-dynamics analyses.

E5.justification: Table 1's uncertainty entries, Appendix C.3's three-random-seed disclosure, and Figure 10's error bars from three independent runs are unchanged. No repeated-run or statistical-reporting practice is revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain all numerical entries, and Figures 2–17 retain their plotted results and qualitative examples. For instance, F-CAGrad's CelebA average error remains 8.22 in Table 2, and F-IMTL's NYUv2 Δm% entry remains -4.77 in Table 4.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 and the main-text derivations are unchanged, as are Theorems 2–4 and their proofs in Appendix A. The mathematical definitions in Appendices B and D.2 are also retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution paragraph and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about task-based flat regions, generalization, gradient conflict, robustness and calibration.

C2.justification: The explanations linking flatness to generalization and calibration are unchanged. Existing qualifications concerning mixed-dataset performance, NYUv2 task tradeoffs and ignored CityScapes regions remain; no substantive interpretation or limitation is added.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains identical implementation details, including architectures, optimizers, learning rates, batch sizes, image resizing and perturbation-radius tuning. No code or data access information is added or revised.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, novelty positioning and all 80 reference entries remain unchanged. Reference-page reflow introduces no citation additions or removals.

P1.justification: v3 adds Quyen Tran and Tuan Truong to the author list, identifies Hoang Phan and Lam Tran as equal contributors, and updates affiliation markers and dates. Scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Existing material is reflowed: Figure 2 moves from page 8 to 9, Table 4 from page 10 to 11, and Figure 5 from page 12 to 13. Table 2 switches sides beside the CelebA discussion. Display contents and captions remain unchanged, and appendix layouts are identical.

improvement.justification: v3 updates authorship information and repositions existing material while preserving the scientific exposition, theoretical arguments, empirical evidence and reproducibility details, including the complete appendices. These limited presentation changes leave overall clarity and scientific support materially equivalent.
